description: This topic explores how biological knowledge and biotechnology are applied in food production, preservation, agriculture, medicine, waste treatment and energy generation, together with the benefits and ethical concerns of modern biotechnology.

options.text: The study of how living organisms grow without any human use
The use of living organisms or their parts to make useful products or processes
The branch of physics that studies machines used in farming
The chemical treatment of minerals to produce fertilisers

mcq.explanation: Biotechnology is the application of living organisms, cells or their components (such as enzymes) to make products like bread, yoghurt, antibiotics and biogas, or to carry out useful processes.

mcq.questionText: Which group of microorganisms is mainly responsible for the rising of bread dough?

options.text: Yeast
Viruses
Protozoa
Algae

mcq.explanation: Yeast is a fungus that ferments sugars in dough, producing carbon dioxide gas that makes the dough rise and become light.

mcq.questionText: During the making of bread, yeast produces carbon dioxide. What is the main role of this gas?

options.text: It kills bacteria in the flour
It adds sweetness to the bread
It forms bubbles that make the dough rise and become soft
It hardens the crust of the bread

mcq.explanation: Carbon dioxide released during fermentation gets trapped in the dough, forming bubbles that cause it to rise and give bread its light, spongy texture.

mcq.questionText: Which microorganisms are used to convert milk into yoghurt?

options.text: Lactic acid bacteria
Yeast cells
Moulds
Viruses

mcq.explanation: Lactic acid bacteria ferment the milk sugar (lactose) into lactic acid, which thickens the milk and gives yoghurt its sour taste.

mcq.questionText: The souring and thickening of milk during yoghurt making is caused by the production of:

options.text: Ethanol
Lactic acid
Carbon dioxide
Citric acid

mcq.explanation: Bacteria ferment lactose into lactic acid; the acid lowers the pH, causing milk proteins to coagulate, which thickens the milk and gives a sour flavour.

mcq.questionText: In brewing of traditional beer such as 'mbege' or 'ulanzi', which substance is mainly produced by fermentation?

options.text: Lactic acid
Ethanol (alcohol)
Vinegar
Methane

mcq.explanation: Yeast ferments the sugars in the brew anaerobically, producing ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide, which is the basis of brewing alcoholic drinks.

mcq.questionText: Which food preservation method works mainly by removing water so that microorganisms cannot grow?

options.text: Drying
Canning
Refrigeration
Pickling

mcq.explanation: Drying (for example sun-drying fish or cassava) removes water from food. Microorganisms need water to grow, so without it they cannot multiply and spoil the food.

mcq.questionText: How does salting preserve food such as fish?

options.text: It supplies extra nutrients to the food
It draws water out of the food and from microbial cells by osmosis
It raises the temperature of the food
It coats the food with a layer that adds vitamins

mcq.explanation: Salt creates a high solute concentration outside microbial cells, drawing water out by osmosis and dehydrating both the food and any microorganisms, preventing their growth.

mcq.questionText: Refrigeration preserves food mainly because low temperatures:

options.text: Kill all microorganisms immediately
Slow down the activity and reproduction of microorganisms and enzymes
Remove all water from the food
Add preservative chemicals to the food

mcq.explanation: Cold temperatures do not usually kill microbes but greatly slow their growth and the enzyme reactions that cause spoilage, so food stays fresh longer.

mcq.questionText: Which preservation method uses an acidic solution such as vinegar to keep food from spoiling?

options.text: Smoking
Canning
Pickling
Freezing

mcq.explanation: Pickling preserves food in an acidic medium (usually vinegar or brine). The low pH prevents the growth of most spoilage microorganisms.

mcq.questionText: Which microorganisms are used to produce most antibiotics such as penicillin?

options.text: Viruses and protozoa
Fungi and bacteria
Algae and ferns
Insects and worms

mcq.explanation: Many antibiotics are made by fungi (for example Penicillium produces penicillin) and certain bacteria. They are grown in large fermenters to produce the medicine.

mcq.questionText: By means of genetic engineering, human insulin for treating diabetes is now produced using:

options.text: Bacteria carrying the human insulin gene
Glands removed from healthy people
Chemical mixing of sugars in a laboratory
Yeast eaten directly by patients

mcq.explanation: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria, which then make human insulin as they multiply. This provides a large, pure and reliable supply for diabetic patients.

mcq.questionText: What is the main role of microorganisms in sewage treatment?

options.text: They add colour to the water
They break down (decompose) organic waste into simpler harmless substances
They increase the amount of waste in the water
They turn the sewage into salt

mcq.explanation: Bacteria and other decomposers feed on the organic matter in sewage, breaking it down into simpler, less harmful substances and making the water safer before release.

mcq.questionText: Biogas produced from animal dung and other organic waste is mainly composed of:

options.text: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide only
Methane
Nitrogen

mcq.explanation: Biogas is mostly methane (with some carbon dioxide) produced when bacteria break down organic waste anaerobically. Methane is the flammable gas used for cooking and lighting.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of biological pest control in agriculture?

options.text: Spraying crops with synthetic chemical pesticides
Using natural enemies such as ladybirds to feed on crop pests
Burning the whole field after harvest
Adding more chemical fertiliser to the soil

mcq.explanation: Biological pest control uses living organisms, such as predatory insects (for example ladybirds eating aphids), to reduce pest populations instead of chemical pesticides.

fib.questionText: The use of living organisms or their parts to make useful products is called _____.
fib.explanation: Biotechnology applies living organisms or their components to produce goods such as bread, yoghurt, medicines and biogas.

fib.questionText: The microorganism added to flour and water to make bread rise is _____.
fib.explanation: Yeast ferments sugars in the dough, releasing carbon dioxide that makes the bread rise.

fib.questionText: The gas produced by yeast that makes bread dough rise is _____.
fib.explanation: Carbon dioxide from fermentation forms bubbles in the dough, making the bread light and spongy.

fib.questionText: The acid produced by bacteria that turns milk into yoghurt is _____ acid.
fib.explanation: Lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose into lactic acid, which sours and thickens the milk.

fib.questionText: The breakdown of sugars by microorganisms in the absence of oxygen is called _____.
fib.explanation: Fermentation is anaerobic respiration by microbes, producing substances such as ethanol or lactic acid.

fib.questionText: Preserving food by removing water through exposure to the sun or heat is called _____.
fib.explanation: Drying removes water needed by microorganisms, preventing them from growing and spoiling the food.

fib.questionText: Salting preserves food because salt draws water out of microbial cells by the process of _____.
fib.explanation: The high salt concentration outside the cells causes water to leave by osmosis, dehydrating and killing the microbes.

fib.questionText: The antibiotic penicillin is obtained from a fungus called _____.
fib.explanation: Penicillium is a mould that produces penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic.

fib.questionText: The flammable gas produced when bacteria break down organic waste without oxygen to form biogas is _____.
fib.explanation: Methane is the main combustible component of biogas, used for cooking and lighting.

fib.questionText: Growing whole plants from a few cells or tissues in a sterile nutrient medium is a technique called _____.
fib.explanation: Tissue culture produces many identical, disease-free plants quickly from small pieces of plant tissue.

tf.questionText: Biotechnology only involves modern laboratory techniques and was never practised in the past.
tf.explanation: Biotechnology is very old; traditional practices like making bread, beer and fermented foods are forms of biotechnology used long before modern laboratories.

tf.questionText: Yeast carries out fermentation that releases carbon dioxide to make bread dough rise.
tf.explanation: Yeast ferments sugars in the dough and the carbon dioxide produced causes the dough to rise.

tf.questionText: Lactic acid bacteria are used to make both yoghurt and cheese.
tf.explanation: Lactic acid bacteria ferment milk in the production of yoghurt and also play a role in making many cheeses.

tf.questionText: Refrigeration kills all microorganisms in food immediately.
tf.explanation: Refrigeration only slows down microbial growth and enzyme activity; it does not kill all the microorganisms.

tf.questionText: Smoking preserves food partly because chemicals in the smoke help prevent the growth of microorganisms.
tf.explanation: Smoke contains drying heat and chemicals (such as those with antimicrobial properties) that help preserve foods like fish and meat.

tf.questionText: Antibiotics are effective medicines for killing viruses such as those causing the common cold.
tf.explanation: Antibiotics act against bacteria, not viruses. They cannot cure viral infections such as the common cold.

tf.questionText: Vaccines work by stimulating the body to produce immunity against a particular disease.
tf.explanation: A vaccine introduces weakened or harmless parts of a pathogen so the body produces antibodies and immune memory, protecting against future infection.

tf.questionText: Genetic engineering allows a useful gene from one organism to be transferred into another organism.
tf.explanation: Genetic engineering involves transferring genes between organisms, for example inserting the human insulin gene into bacteria.

tf.questionText: Biogas can be produced from animal dung and other organic waste using microorganisms.
tf.explanation: Bacteria break down organic waste anaerobically in a digester to produce biogas (mainly methane) used for cooking and lighting.

tf.questionText: Some people raise ethical and safety concerns about genetically modified organisms (GMOs).
tf.explanation: Modern biotechnology, especially GMOs, raises concerns about safety, environmental effects and ethics, which is why it is debated and regulated.

summary.questionText: Define biotechnology and give two everyday examples.
summary.correctAnswer: Biotechnology is the use of living organisms or their parts to make useful products or processes. Everyday examples include using yeast to make bread and using bacteria to make yoghurt.
summary.explanation: The definition stresses the use of living organisms; bread-making and yoghurt-making are familiar, traditional examples.

summary.questionText: Explain how yeast is used in the making of bread.
summary.correctAnswer: Yeast is mixed into the dough where it ferments sugars in the absence of oxygen. This fermentation produces carbon dioxide gas, which forms bubbles that make the dough rise and become light and spongy.
summary.explanation: The key points are fermentation of sugars by yeast and the release of carbon dioxide that causes the dough to rise.

summary.questionText: Describe how milk is turned into yoghurt by microorganisms.
summary.correctAnswer: Lactic acid bacteria are added to warm milk. They ferment the milk sugar (lactose) into lactic acid. The acid lowers the pH, causing the milk proteins to coagulate, which thickens the milk and gives yoghurt its sour taste.
summary.explanation: The answer connects bacterial fermentation of lactose to lactic acid, and the acid to thickening and souring.

summary.questionText: List four methods of food preservation.
summary.correctAnswer: Four methods of food preservation are drying, salting, smoking and refrigeration. Other methods include canning and pickling.
summary.explanation: These are the common preservation methods that prevent or slow microbial growth and spoilage.

summary.questionText: Explain the biological reason why drying and salting are able to preserve food.
summary.correctAnswer: Microorganisms need water to grow and multiply. Drying removes water from the food, while salting draws water out of the food and from microbial cells by osmosis. Without enough water, microorganisms cannot grow and spoil the food.
summary.explanation: Both methods work by reducing the water available to microbes, drying directly and salting through osmosis.

summary.questionText: State three applications of biology and biotechnology in agriculture.
summary.correctAnswer: Applications in agriculture include the use of improved seeds and breeds for higher yield, the use of biofertilisers to improve soil fertility, biological pest control using natural enemies of pests, and tissue culture to produce many disease-free plants.
summary.explanation: These examples show how biological knowledge improves crop and animal production.

summary.questionText: Describe three uses of biotechnology in medicine.
summary.correctAnswer: In medicine, microorganisms are grown to produce antibiotics such as penicillin; vaccines are made to protect people against diseases; and genetic engineering is used to produce human insulin from bacteria for treating diabetes.
summary.explanation: Antibiotics, vaccines and insulin production are key medical applications of biotechnology.

summary.questionText: Explain the role of microorganisms in sewage and waste treatment.
summary.correctAnswer: In sewage and waste treatment, bacteria and other decomposers feed on the organic matter in the waste. They break it down into simpler, harmless substances, reducing pollution and making the water safer before it is released into the environment.
summary.explanation: The answer highlights decomposition of organic waste by microorganisms into harmless products.

summary.questionText: Describe how biogas is produced and state one of its uses.
summary.correctAnswer: Biogas is produced when bacteria break down organic waste such as animal dung in a digester in the absence of oxygen. This anaerobic decomposition produces a flammable gas that is mainly methane. Biogas is used as a fuel for cooking and lighting.
summary.explanation: The key ideas are anaerobic breakdown of organic waste by bacteria, production of methane, and its use as fuel.

summary.questionText: State two benefits and two concerns of modern biotechnology such as genetic engineering.
summary.correctAnswer: Benefits include the production of important medicines such as insulin and the development of crops with higher yields or pest resistance. Concerns include possible unknown effects on human health and the environment, and ethical issues about altering the genes of living things.
summary.explanation: A balanced answer gives clear benefits (medicines, improved crops) and concerns (health, environmental and ethical issues).

hoq.questionText: A farmer notices that aphids are destroying her vegetable garden, but she wants to avoid using chemical pesticides that harm the soil and beneficial insects. Which approach best applies biological knowledge to solve her problem?

options.text: Spray the whole garden with a strong chemical insecticide every day
Introduce ladybirds, which are natural predators that feed on aphids
Burn all the vegetables to remove the aphids
Add large amounts of chemical fertiliser to the soil

hoq.explanation: This is biological pest control: introducing a natural enemy (ladybirds) to reduce the pest (aphids) without harming the soil or beneficial insects, unlike chemical spraying.

hoq.questionText: A scientist wants to produce a large, pure and reliable supply of human insulin to treat many diabetic patients. Which method makes the best use of biotechnology to achieve this?

options.text: Insert the human insulin gene into bacteria and grow them in fermenters
Collect insulin from the blood of healthy volunteers
Mix sugars and salts together in a laboratory to form insulin
Feed diabetic patients large amounts of yeast

hoq.explanation: Genetic engineering inserts the human insulin gene into bacteria, which then make human insulin as they multiply in fermenters, giving a large, pure and reliable supply.

hoq.questionText: A rural family produces a lot of cow dung and crop waste and also struggles to afford firewood and kerosene for cooking. How can they use biotechnology to solve both problems at once?

options.text: Dry the dung and waste and store it without using it
Burn the dung directly to make more smoke for cooking
Build a biogas digester so bacteria break down the waste anaerobically to produce methane fuel
Bury the waste deep underground to remove the smell

hoq.explanation: A biogas digester lets bacteria break down the dung and crop waste without oxygen, producing methane gas for cooking and lighting while also managing the waste, solving both problems.
